Overview / Operations / Tasks & Assignments
Operational tasking

Make the assignment clear before the team moves.

A task keeps the objective, location, assigned resource, supervisor, and operational constraints together. As the work proceeds, status and field reporting remain connected to that same assignment.

The task record

One place for the work to be done.

A useful assignment answers who, what, where, when, and what result is expected. It also gives the team enough context to act without searching through unrelated incident records.

Objective
Purpose and expected result
Location
Area, map geometry, and access
Assignment
Team and supervisor
Constraints
Hazards, timing, and communications
Record
Status, narrative, and outcome
Task progress

Follow the work, not just the dispatch.

Task status describes progress on the assignment. Team status describes the resource carrying it out; the two move together but answer different questions.

PlannedDefine the work and the area.
AssignedAttach the team and supervisor.
In progressFollow field updates and changes.
CompleteRecord result and any follow-up.
Geographic context

The map travels with the assignment.

A task can carry a planning segment, search area, route, hazard, or other operational feature. That geography is available to the field team and remains linked to the resulting report.

Explore mapping & GIS →
What comes back

Close the loop with the field result.

Status and narrative updates, observations, clues, and hazards can change what the next team needs to do. Keep the outcome with the task and feed actionable findings into planning.

Field reporting →Planning →Incident logs →
How a task connects

The assignment carries more than instructions.

INPUTIntelligenceA lead or clue establishes a new need.PLACEMappingThe area, route, and hazards travel with the task.ACTIONField appThe team reports progress and findings.RESULTPlanningResults change the next allocation of work.

The task stays linked to its team, map features, and narrative entries throughout that path.
